passages.text: On the other side of the sea, they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples crossed the sea.
They reached the other side.
They arrived in the region called the Gerasenes.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν

passages.text: As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, He was met by a man with an unclean spirit, who was coming from the tombs.
passages.sermon:
Jesus got out of the boat.
A man met Jesus immediately.
This man came from the tombs.
An unclean spirit possessed the man.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ

passages.text: This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained, even with chains.
passages.sermon:
A man met Jesus.
This man lived among the tombs.
No one could restrain him anymore.
Even chains could not hold him.
passages.original: ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι

passages.text: Though he was often bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and shattered the shackles. Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him.
passages.sermon:
The man had an unclean spirit.
People often bound him with chains and shackles.
He broke the chains by his own strength.
He shattered the shackles.
No one was strong enough to subdue him.
passages.original: διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσιν δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι

passages.text: Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.
passages.sermon:
This man lived among the tombs and in the mountains.
He was there all the time, both night and day.
He cried out loudly again and again.
He cut himself with stones.
passages.original: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις

passages.text: When the man saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees before Him.
passages.sermon:
A man lived among the tombs and mountains.
He was possessed by many unclean spirits.
No one could subdue him.
He often broke chains and shackles.
He cried out night and day.
He cut himself with stones.
One day, the man saw Jesus from far away.
He ran toward Jesus.
He fell on his knees before Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν

passages.text: And he shouted in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!”
passages.sermon:
A man lived among the tombs and mountains.
He was possessed by many unclean spirits.
He saw Jesus from a distance.
He ran to Jesus.
He fell on his knees before Jesus.
He shouted with a loud voice.
He said, “What do you want with me, Jesus?”
He called Jesus the Son of the Most High God.
He begged Jesus by God.
He said, “Do not torture me.”
passages.original: καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί Ἰησοῦ Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου ὁρκίζω σε τὸν Θεόν μή με βασανίσῃς

passages.text: For Jesus had already declared, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the unclean spirit.\r\nJesus commanded the spirit.\r\nJesus said, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit.”
passages.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “My name is Legion,” he replied, “for we are many.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus asked, “What is your name?”
The man answered Jesus.
He said, “My name is Legion.”
He said this because many demons were inside him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν Τί ὄνομά σοι Καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν

passages.text: And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region.
passages.sermon:
A man had many unclean spirits inside him.
Jesus spoke to the unclean spirits.
The unclean spirits begged Jesus many times.
They asked Jesus not to send them out of that region.
passages.original: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας

passages.text: There on the nearby hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding.
passages.sermon: A large herd of pigs was on the hillside.\r\nThe pigs were feeding there.\r\nThe hillside was nearby.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη

passages.text: So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”
passages.sermon:
The demons spoke to Jesus.
They begged Jesus.
They said, “Send us to the pigs.”
They wanted to enter the pigs.
They asked Jesus for permission to go into the pigs.
passages.original: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν

passages.text: He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood there.
A large herd of pigs was nearby.
The herd had about two thousand pigs.
Unclean spirits were present.
Jesus gave the unclean spirits permission to leave the man.
The unclean spirits came out of the man.
The unclean spirits entered the pigs.
The pigs rushed down the steep bank.
The pigs ran into the sea.
All the pigs drowned in the water.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ὡς δισχίλιοι καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ

passages.text: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.
passages.sermon:
Some men were taking care of the pigs.
These men saw what happened.
They ran away quickly.
They went into the town.
They also went into the countryside.
They told people what had happened.
Many people heard the news.
The people wanted to see for themselves.
They went out to see what had happened.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός

passages.text: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
passages.sermon:
The people came to Jesus.
They saw the man who had been possessed by many demons.
This man had been called the one with the legion.
He was sitting down.
He was wearing clothes.
He was in his right mind.
The people became afraid.
passages.original: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν

passages.text: Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.
passages.sermon:
Some people saw what happened.
These people told others about it.
They explained what happened to the man who had been possessed by demons.
They also explained what happened to the pigs.
passages.original: καὶ διηγήσαντο αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων

passages.text: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.
passages.sermon:
The people saw Jesus.
They saw what He had done.
They began to beg Jesus.
They asked Him to leave their region.
passages.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν

passages.text: As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was getting into the boat.
A man had been possessed by demons.
This man begged Jesus.
He asked to go with Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα μετ’ αὐτοῦ ᾖ

passages.text: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man who had been possessed by demons.
Jesus did not allow the man to go with Him.
Jesus said, “Go home to your own people.”
Jesus said, “Tell them what the Lord has done for you.”
Jesus said, “Tell them how the Lord has shown you mercy.”
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς καὶ ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ὁ Κύριός σοι πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε

passages.text: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.
passages.sermon:
The man had been possessed by demons.
Jesus had healed him.
The man went away.
He began to proclaim in the Decapolis.
He told people what Jesus had done for him.
Everyone heard his message.
Everyone was amazed.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον

passages.text: When Jesus had again crossed by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him beside the sea.
passages.sermon: Jesus crossed to the other side by boat.\r\nA large crowd gathered around Jesus.\r\nThey stood beside the sea.
passages.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ πάλιν εἰς τὸ πέραν συνήχθη ὄχλος πολὺς ἐπ’ αὐτόν καὶ ἦν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν

passages.text: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived, and seeing Jesus, he fell at His feet and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”
passages.sermon:
Jairus was a synagogue leader.
Jairus came to Jesus.
Jairus saw Jesus.
Jairus fell at Jesus’ feet.
Jairus pleaded with Jesus urgently.
Jairus said, “My little daughter is near death.”
Jairus asked Jesus, “Please come.”
Jairus asked Jesus, “Place Your hands on her.”
Jairus said, “Then she will be healed.”
Jairus said, “Then she will live.”
passages.original: καὶ ἔρχεται εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων ὀνόματι Ἰάϊρος καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν πίπτει πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ παρακαλεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ λέγων ὅτι Τὸ θυγάτριόν μου ἐσχάτως ἔχει ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ ἵνα σωθῇ καὶ ζήσῃ

passages.text: So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus went with Jairus.\r\nA large crowd followed Jesus.\r\nThe crowd pressed closely around Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς καὶ συνέθλιβον αὐτόν

passages.text: And a woman was there who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
passages.sermon: A woman stood in the crowd.\r\nShe had suffered from bleeding.\r\nHer bleeding had lasted twelve years.
passages.original: Καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος δώδεκα ἔτη

passages.text: She had borne much agony under the care of many physicians and had spent all she had, but to no avail. Instead, her condition had only grown worse.
passages.sermon:
The woman suffered greatly.
Many doctors treated her.
She spent all her money.
The doctors did not help her.
Her condition became worse.
passages.original: καὶ πολλὰ παθοῦσα ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἰατρῶν καὶ δαπανήσασα τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς πάντα καὶ μηδὲν ὠφεληθεῖσα ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐλθοῦσα

passages.text: When the woman heard about Jesus, she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak.
passages.sermon:
A woman had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She heard about Jesus.
She came up behind Jesus in the crowd.
She touched His cloak.
passages.original: ἀκούσασα τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ

passages.text: For she kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.”
passages.sermon:
A woman suffered for many years.
She had a bleeding condition.
She spent all her money on doctors.
No doctor could heal her.
Her condition became worse.
She heard about Jesus.
She believed Jesus could heal her.
She said, “If I touch His garments, I will be healed.”
She kept saying this to herself.
She believed touching Jesus’ clothes would heal her.
passages.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὅτι Ἐὰν ἅψωμαι κἂν τῶν ἱματίων αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι

passages.text: Immediately her bleeding stopped, and she sensed in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
passages.sermon:
A woman suffered from bleeding for many years.
She touched Jesus’ cloak in the crowd.
Immediately, her bleeding stopped.
She felt in her body that she was healed.
She knew she was free from her suffering.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξηράνθη ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς καὶ ἔγνω τῷ σώματι ὅτι ἴαται ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος

passages.text: At once Jesus was aware that power had gone out from Him. Turning to the crowd, He asked, “Who touched My garments?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nHe stood among a large crowd.
\r\nImmediately, Jesus knew something had happened.
\r\nHe felt power go out from Himself.
\r\nJesus turned to the people around Him.
\r\nHe asked, “Who touched My garments?”
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπιγνοὺς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐπιστραφεὶς ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ἔλεγεν Τίς μου ἥψατο τῶν ἱματίων

passages.text: His disciples answered, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus had many disciples.
His disciples spoke to Him.
They said, “You see the crowd around You.
The people are pressing against You.
Yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Βλέπεις τὸν ὄχλον συνθλίβοντά σε καὶ λέγεις Τίς μου ἥψατο

passages.text: But He kept looking around to see who had done this.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood in the crowd.
He looked around carefully.
He wanted to see who had touched His garments.
He searched for the person who had done this.
passages.original: Καὶ περιεβλέπετο ἰδεῖν τὴν τοῦτο ποιήσασαν

passages.text: Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him trembling in fear, and she told Him the whole truth.
passages.sermon:
A woman had just been healed by Jesus.
She knew what had happened to her.
She felt afraid.
She trembled.
She came to Jesus.
She fell down before Him.
She told Him the whole truth.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ φοβηθεῖσα καὶ τρέμουσα εἰδυῖα ὃ γέγονεν αὐτῇ ἦλθεν καὶ προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν

passages.text: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He called her "Daughter."
He said, "Your faith has healed you."
He told her, "Go in peace."
He said, "Be free from your affliction."
The woman had suffered from a disease.
Her faith in Jesus made her well.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Θυγάτηρ ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε ὕπαγε εἰς εἰρήνην καὶ ἴσθι ὑγιὴς ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγός σου

passages.text: While He was still speaking, messengers from the house of Jairus arrived and said, “Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was still speaking.
Messengers came from the house of Jairus.
Jairus was the synagogue leader.
The messengers spoke to Jairus.
They said, “Your daughter is dead.”
They also said, “Do not trouble the Teacher any longer.”
passages.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ σου ἀπέθανεν τί ἔτι σκύλλεις τὸν διδάσκαλον

passages.text: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard what the messengers said.
Jairus was the leader of the synagogue.
Jesus spoke to Jairus.
Jesus said, “Do not be afraid.”
Jesus said, “Only believe.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς παρακούσας τὸν λόγον λαλούμενον λέγει τῷ ἀρχισυναγώγῳ Μὴ φοβοῦ μόνον πίστευε

passages.text: And He did not allow anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was the Son of God and the Teacher.
\r\nHe was going to the house of Jairus, the synagogue leader.
\r\nJesus did not allow anyone to go with Him.
\r\nHe allowed only three men to go with Him.
\r\nThese men were Peter, James, and John.
\r\nJohn was the brother of James.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν οὐδένα μετ’ αὐτοῦ συνακολουθῆσαι εἰ μὴ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰακώβου

passages.text: When they arrived at the house of the synagogue leader, Jesus saw the commotion and the people weeping and wailing loudly.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
They came to the house of Jairus.
Jairus was the leader of the synagogue.
Jesus saw a commotion in the house.
Many people were there.
The people were weeping.
The people were wailing loudly.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου καὶ θεωρεῖ θόρυβον καὶ κλαίοντας καὶ ἀλαλάζοντας πολλά

passages.text: He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader.
He saw the people making a commotion.
He saw them weeping.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Why are you making this commotion?”
He said, “Why are you weeping?”
He said, “The child is not dead.”
He said, “The child is asleep.”
passages.original: καὶ εἰσελθὼν λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί θορυβεῖσθε καὶ κλαίετε τὸ παιδίον οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει

passages.text: And they laughed at Him. After He had put them all outside, He took the child’s father and mother and His own companions, and went in to see the child.
passages.sermon:
The people laughed at Jesus.
Jesus put everyone outside.
Jesus took the child’s father.
Jesus took the child’s mother.
Jesus took His own companions.
Jesus went in to where the child was.
passages.original: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκβαλὼν πάντας παραλαμβάνει τὸν πατέρα τοῦ παιδίου καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τοὺς μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσπορεύεται ὅπου ἦν τὸ παιδίον

passages.text: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus took the girl's hand.
He spoke to her.
He said, "Talitha koum!"
This means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up!"
passages.original: καὶ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου λέγει αὐτῇ Ταλιθὰ κούμ ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Τὸ Κοράσιον σοὶ λέγω ἔγειρε

passages.text: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around. She was twelve years old, and at once they were utterly astounded.
passages.sermon:
The girl was twelve years old.
She got up immediately.
She began to walk around.
Everyone saw this happen.
They were all completely amazed.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέστη τὸ κοράσιον καὶ περιεπάτει ἦν γὰρ ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ ἐξέστησαν εὐθὺς ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ

passages.text: Then Jesus gave strict orders that no one should know about this, and He told them to give her something to eat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people there.
He gave them strict orders.
He told them not to let anyone know what had happened.
He told them to give the girl something to eat.
passages.original: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἵνα μηδεὶς γνοῖ τοῦτο καὶ εἶπεν δοθῆναι αὐτῇ φαγεῖν
